title: What is known about 1RB0LA_1RC---_0LD1RD_0RA0RE_0RF1RC_1LF0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_1RC---_0LD1RD_0RA0RE_0RF1RC_1LF0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. It is one of three G13 holdouts with the same behaviour (the others are 1RB0LA_1RC---_0LD1RD_0RB0RE_0RF0LD_1LF0LA and 1RB1RF_0RC1RD_1LC1LA_0LE1RE_1RA0RB_---0LC): a solid wall of 1s that grows to the right by 3 cells every time the head comes back to it, and in front of it a short list of blocks of 1s that the head rewrites on every pass, following a recursive rule found from the simulation and checked on more than a million passes. This page says what that rule is, what is checked, and what is still open.
verdict: The question is open. The run is understood at the level of passes: between two visits of the head to the wall the list of blocks changes by a short recursive rule, and every one of the 1,311,505 wall visits in the first 109 steps follows it (C simulator plus py/passmap.py, not a proof). The rule itself never halts; what is not understood is the rare pass in which the list reaches the wall, where in the sibling machine 1RB0LA_1RC---_0LD1RD_0RB0RE_0RF0LD_1LF0LA the whole structure collapses and restarts. Lean proves the bounded runs, that the machine halts if and only if the run reaches D>0 0 1, and the pass rule itself for every list in the cases that do not involve the wall or the shape 2 0 1 Y (96.9% of the passes of the first 109 steps).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,954,386 cells have been visited and 3,954,346 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/linear
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 0.95).

claims.title: The pass map holds for the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: Each time the head, in state D, stands just right of the wall (a run of at least 1000 1s followed by one 0), the tape right of the wall is a list of blocks 1^(3k) 0 (k = 0 meaning an extra 0) and a tail 1^(7+3j). Of these visits in the first 109 steps, 1,311,505 follow the pass map of the README from the previous visit: 1,311,477 after one pass, 28 after two or three (the head came back to the wall in another state in between, unseen by the sampler). 4 passes reach the wall itself, where the map does not apply. At step 999,999,9xx the wall has 3,954,209 cells and the list is 4 2 1 1 1 2 1 1 8 1 1 1 3 1 1 1 1 3 1 2 1 1 T5.

claims.title: The same map for three machines
claims.text: The same pass map, with the same list notation, describes 1RB0LA_1RC---_0LD1RD_0RB0RE_0RF0LD_1LF0LA and 1RB1RF_0RC1RD_1LC1LA_0LE1RE_1RA0RB_---0LC; only the starting list, the state in which the head meets the wall and the tail offset differ (1^(7+3j) here).

claims.title: Two encodings of the same list
claims.text: On the way right the head rewrites each block 1^(3k) 0 as 1^3 0 (1^2 0)^(k-1) (same width), and on the way back it rewrites it again; only the end of the list, and the place of the first empty block, change from pass to pass.

claims.title: The leftward rewrite, for every n
claims.text: From L 111 (110)^n … written as L (110)^n 111 B>000 R, the machine reaches L 111 B>000 (111)^n R in exactly 11n steps, for any tapes L and R: one 11-step unit L 110 111 B>000 R → L 111 B>000 111 R (generated by symtm) chained by induction.

claims.title: The only way to halt
claims.text: The run from blank tape halts if and only if it reaches a configuration D>0 0 1 (the head in state D on a 0, with these cells to its right). B is entered only by A0 = 1RB; A is entered by A1 and F1, which move left and leave a 0 right of the head, and by D0 = 0RA. So the halt is D>0 0 1, 0 A>0 1, 0 1 B>1. The proof is an invariant of the run: while no such configuration has occurred, A on a 0 has a 0 on its right and B reads a 0.

claims.title: State D reads a 0 only 25 times in 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: In the first 109 steps the head is in state D on a 0 exactly 25 times: 11 times with 0 0 0 to its right (first at step 42, last at step 20,653,972) and 14 times with 1 1 1 (first at step 262, last at step 4,054,180); the critical 0 1 never follows. All 25 fall in the starts and restarts of the structure (steps up to 2,740, 3,775,216 to 4,370,514, then 13,579,469 and 20,653,972); in the passes that follow the pass map D always reads a 1.

claims.title: Both sweeps of a pass, for every list
claims.text: For every list of blocks and any tapes on both sides: state D crosses the blocks 1 0 1 1 (111)^j (the list as D meets it) to the right and leaves 0 111 (011)^j for each; state A at 0 000 crosses those back to the left and leaves 0 1^(3j+3) for each, the cursor A>0 000 travelling along. Proved from four fixed runs (3, 6, 11 and 12 steps) by induction on the block size and on the list.

claims.title: The pass relation is sound, for every list and every left tape
claims.text: A visit is L 0 D>1 0 k1 … kn X with any tape L on the left. Lean defines a relation Reach on lists with seven rules (sweep over a block; bounce: n 0 1 Y becomes (n−2) 1 2 and the sweep goes on into Y, for n ≥ 3; and five ends: … Tj → … j T0, … T0 → … 0 T0, … n 0 T0 → … (n−2) 1 1 T0 for n ≥ 3, … 2 0 T0 → … 0 1 1 T0, and … a 1 0 X → … [1^(3a+3) X] for any tape X) and proves: every derivation is a run of the machine from the visit to the next visit, with three more 1s on the left (the wall grows by 3). This holds for every list and every L, so it covers the recursion of the pass map. No rule exists yet for 2 0 1 Y (an empty block with a 2 on its left and a block after it), nor for an empty block (or 1 0) at the very start of the list, where the wall takes part.

claims.title: The proved passes cover 96.9% of the wall visits in 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: Of the 1,311,509 pairs of consecutive wall visits in the first 109 steps, 1,270,317 are exactly one pass derivable in the proved relation (460,247 ending with the new empty block, 321,518 with a merge, 243,654 with the tail splitting off, 122,579 with a split, 122,319 with the split of a block of size 2) and 27 are two or three such passes in a row (visits between them not recorded). Not covered: 41,162 pairs of the shape 2 0 1 Y, and 3 where 1 0 stands at the wall. No pair contradicts the relation.

claims.title: The arrival rule needs only two 0s
claims.where: wall_turn, lean/PassTail.lean (the rule); the reading of it is a conjecture
claims.text: Proved: the arrival 0 A>0 000 0 X → 111 0 D>1 0 X (15 steps) holds with any tape on the left, wall or not. Conjecture drawn from it, not checked: when a pass leaves an empty block inside the list and the sweep goes on to the right of it (the case 2 0 1 Y), the returning sweep turns at that empty block and a new pass starts on the right part alone, which would be how a wall starts and why py/passmap.py sees some visits only after two or three passes.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Lean reduces the question to one pattern (the machine halts if and only if the run reaches D>0 0 1) and proves most of the pass map for every list (pass_sound). Missing for a non-halting proof: the rule for 2 0 1 Y and the rules for an empty block at the wall (where the wall, or an older structure behind it, takes part), and an invariant: a description of all lists, walls and debris the run can reach, closed under all rules, in which D never meets 0 0 1. Only three restarts have been seen in 109 steps, so that invariant has to be derived from the rules, not fitted to data.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The machine builds a solid wall of 1s that grows by 3 cells per pass, and in front of it the head shuttles over a short list of blocks that changes like a counter whose digits are counters. This page shows the rule and how far it has been checked.

of the passes in 10<sup>9</sup> steps follow rules proved in Lean for every list (the count itself is a computation)
the wall grows by 3 cells per pass; the list stays short

sections.heading: A wall, a list and a shuttle
html: After a short start the tape always has the same three parts: some debris on the far left (1^3 0 1^2 0 1^5 0 1^1322 0 1^2 0), a solid wall of 1s that keeps growing, and right of the wall a short list of blocks of 1s that ends in a slightly longer block, the tail. The head shuttles between the wall and the end of the list. Every time it comes back to the wall, the wall is 3 cells longer: after 109 steps it has 3,954,209 cells while the list right of it is only 161 cells long.

Stop the simulation each time the head stands just right of the wall. Then every block of the list is a run of 1s whose length is a multiple of 3, 1^(3k), followed by one 0; a block with k = 0 is just an extra 0. The tail is 1^(7+3j). Write the list as numbers: the tape 1^9 0 1^3 0 0 1^3 0 1^3 0 1^7 is 3 1 0 1 1 T0.

On the way right the head rewrites each block 1^(3k) 0 as 1^3 0 1^2 0 … 1^2 0 (one 3 and k−1 2s, the same number of cells), and on the way back it turns it into 1^(3k) 0 again. So most of the list is just carried along; what changes is decided at one place.

sections.heading: From pass to pass: a counter whose digits are counters
html:
Between two visits to the wall the list changes by this rule (found from the simulation, not yet proved):

  • No empty block in the list: the tail splits off, … Tj → … j T0 if j ≥ 1, and … T0 → … 0 T0 (an empty block is appended).
  • Otherwise look at the first empty block and the number n just left of it, … n 0 X. If n ≥ 2: n 0 X → (n−2) 1 f(X), where f(T0) = 1 T0 and f(1 Y) = 2 step(Y): the part after the empty block takes one step of the same map, as if the empty block were a wall of its own.
  • If n = 1, with a the number before it: a 1 0 T0 → T(a+1) (the tail swallows the block a), and a 1 0 1 Y → (a+2) Y.

Here is the end of the list at seven consecutive visits early in the run of the first machine of the family: 1 1 1 T3, 1 1 1 3 T0, 1 1 1 3 0 T0, 1 1 1 1 1 1 T0, 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 T0, 1 1 1 1 T2, 1 1 1 1 2 T0. The last numbers behave like the low digits of a counter, and the first empty block acts like a small wall for everything after it, so the list is a counter whose digits are themselves counters. Changes deep in the list are rare: in the frequency table of the rules each deeper rule fires about half as often as the one before.

The rule has no branch that halts. It is checked against the machine itself: py/passmap.py runs the C simulator and compares every visit with the rule applied to the previous one. All 1,311,505 visits of the first 109 steps agree.

sections.heading: When the list reaches the wall
html: The rule needs a number left of the first empty block. When the empty block is the first entry, or when a 1 0 has the wall itself as a, the wall takes part in the pass. In the sibling machine 1RB0LA_1RC---_0LD1RD_0RB0RE_0RF0LD_1LF0LA this led, at step 1,858,969, to a collapse: the list became 1 T0, the tail swallowed the wall, and the head swept left over a stack of older walls of lengths 8192, 2048, 512, 128, 32 (each a quarter of the one before), erasing them, before a new wall started growing. So the machine has epochs, and walls of sizes 2·4k point to a regular structure in them.

For this machine, 4 of the passes in the first 109 steps reached the wall. A proof that the machine never halts would need the pass rules proved for every list (an induction on the list in Lean) and a description of what happens at the wall, including the collapses. Neither is done yet.

New in this pass of the analysis: what a collapse looks like in this machine. At the wall visit of step 3,734,901 the list is 0 1 2 2 2 2 2 1 1 1 0 T0 next to a wall of 40,124 cells: the empty block is the first entry. The head then erases the whole wall (at step 3,775,536 there is a run of 40,113 zeros in its place), runs to the left end of the tape and starts again there, as from blank tape, with the old list left far to the right as debris. The new structure grows through the zeros in rounds: at step 4,047,887 the tape holds walls of 1283, 2048, 512, 128, 32 and 8 ones separated by 0 1^2 0, and by step 4,052,252 they have been turned into markers 1^6 0^1279 1^6 0^2046 1^6 0^510 1^6 0^126 1^6 0^30 1^6 0^6 (zero runs 2·4k−2). The head is at the left end for the last time at step 4,053,763 (122 times in 3·109 steps). In the zeros the list runs through shrinking rounds (it merges into the tail as T13, later T11, T9, T7); at step 13,579,469 walls of 32768, 8192, 2048, 512, 128, 32 and 8 ones stand right of the list, and after step 20,653,972 state D reads no 0 again up to 109 steps: a long quiet phase, at whose end the wall has 3,952,883 cells and the list reaches to the right end of the tape. These are observations of one run; no rule for the restarts is known, and a restart is where a halt could come from (see the next section).

sections.heading: One sweep proved for all lengths
html: The unit L 110 111 B>000 R → L 111 B>000 111 R (11 steps) is proved for any surrounding tapes, and unwind chains it n times. This is one piece of the sweeps behind the pass map. The other sweep, the end-of-list rules and the wall passes are not proved yet, so the pass map is still a trusted computation, not a theorem.

sections.heading: The pass map, proved for every list
html: A pass has four parts, and each is now a Lean theorem that holds for every list and every tape left of it. Right sweep: state D turns each block 1^(3k) 0 into 0 111 (011)^(k-1) (read one cell later, the same cells as 1^3 0 (1^2 0)^(k-1)). Turn: at the end of the list or at an empty block a fixed run of 8 to 66 steps rearranges a few cells and leaves the head in state A on a 0 followed by three 0s. Left sweep: with this cursor A>0 000 the head turns every rewritten block into a solid block again, four cells further right. Arrival: at the two 0s before the wall, 15 steps add 111 to the wall and give the next visit 0 D>1 0.

The recursive rule n 0 1 Y → (n−2) 1 2 step(Y) turns out to need no recursion in the proof: at such an empty block the head bounces (19 steps), and the same right sweep simply goes on into Y; the one left sweep at the end crosses everything. In Lean this is an inductive relation Reach with seven rules and the theorem pass_sound: every derivation is a run of the machine from one visit to the next. For example 2 3 0 1 T2 → 2 1 1 2 2 T0 is derived with two sweeps, one bounce and the tail rule, for any wall.

Checked against the run (py/passrel.py): 1,270,317 of the 1,311,509 pairs of consecutive wall visits in 109 steps are exactly one proved pass, and none contradicts the relation. The rest are the cases without a rule yet: the shape 2 0 1 Y, an empty block with a block of size 2 on its left and a block after it (41,162 pairs), and 1 0 at the wall (3 pairs). One proved fact points at what happens there: the arrival rule needs only two 0s, not a wall, so a returning sweep would turn at any empty block it finds inside the list. Whether that is how a wall is born has not been checked.

sections.heading: The one configuration that can halt
html: Lean now proves where a halt has to come from: the run from blank tape halts if and only if it reaches D>0 0 1. B is entered only by A0 = 1RB; A is entered by A1 and F1, which move left and leave a 0 right of the head, and by D0 = 0RA. So the halt is D>0 0 1, 0 A>0 1, 0 1 B>1; every other way into the halting transition is ruled out by a small invariant (while no such configuration has occurred, A on a 0 has a 0 on its right and B reads a 0), checked transition by transition.

In the first 109 steps the head is in state D on a 0 exactly 25 times: 11 times with 0 0 0 to its right (first at step 42, last at step 20,653,972) and 14 times with 1 1 1 (first at step 262, last at step 4,054,180); the critical 0 1 never follows. All 25 fall in the starts and restarts of the structure (steps up to 2,740, 3,775,216 to 4,370,514, then 13,579,469 and 20,653,972); in the passes that follow the pass map D always reads a 1. (C simulator, c/crit.c; a count, not a proof.)
So the open question is exactly whether a restart of the structure can ever put that pattern under the head.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 0.95).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,954,386 cells (81 left of the start, 2,130,084 right), with a density of 1s of 1.0.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: recursive counter riding a growing wall
summary: A solid block grows to the right at one cell per pass; in front of it the head shuttles over a short list of blocks 1^(3k) that changes like a recursive counter, the same pass map as two other G13 machines.
